column1: # Reports whose OWN ARITHMETIC does not close, verified by hand against the page.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR, AND WHAT IT IS NOT FOR
# The extraction is checked by the page's own arithmetic: a province's health
# zone rows, plus any rows the source counts but has not assigned to a zone,
# must equal the province total the page prints. A residual is normally OUR
# defect -- a row the reader failed to recover -- and most chased so far have
# been exactly that, each traceable to one row whose value equalled the gap.
# But some pages do not close on their own terms. An entry here asserts: I
# OPENED THIS PAGE, ADDED THE PRINTED ROWS, AND THE SOURCE DOES NOT AGREE WITH
# ITSELF. It is a claim about the document, not a licence to silence a check.
# Every entry below was read against the rendered page, not inferred from the
# residual's size -- a residual's shape suggests where to look and never what
# is there.
# KEYED ON THE FILE HASH, NOT THE REPORT NUMBER. INSP revises reports and
# republishes them under the same number. An exception granted to one version
# must not silently carry over to a corrected one, so the hash is verified and a
# mismatch fails the build rather than applying a stale exception. `sha256_16`
# is the first 16 hex characters of the file's SHA-256.
# `expected_gap` IS EXACT. The build accepts that residual and no other. If our
# reading later improves or regresses the number changes, and the report returns
# to the failing set instead of staying quietly excused.
# COLUMNS
#   sitrep        report number
#   date          data date, from the page's `Date de rapportage`
#   sha256_16     first 16 hex characters of the PDF's SHA-256
#   unit          which identity: a province name, or `national`
#   column        which value column the exception covers
#   expected_gap  the residual the printed page produces, signed as
#                 (sum of parts) - (printed total)
#   verified_by   who checked, and against what
#   note          what is inconsistent on the page
sitrep

column7: read against the rendered page 2026-08-16: Table 2's Katwa row, Table 2's province row, the provincial summary table, and the narrative paragraph
column8: THE PAGE STATES NORD-KIVU'S CUMULATIVE DEATHS TWO WAYS AND OUR ZONE SUM AGREES WITH THE NARRATIVE. Table 2's province row and the provincial summary both print 290; the narrative reads "Le cumul atteint 426 cas et 288 deces, soit une letalite de 68,1 %", and the twelve zone rows sum to 288. The cases agree everywhere at 426. The same two deaths are visible in the daily block: the narrative says 5 deaths all at Katwa of which 2 in a treatment centre, and the province row prints 3 community plus 2 intra-CTE, while Katwa's own row prints 1 community plus 2 intra-CTE. The zone row is two community deaths short of what the province row and the narrative both assert.
